title: Commercial Credit Account Standing and the Stock-Rotation Allowance
content:
**Credit standing share — Ship-To Fulfillment Account stock-rotation returns.**

> The gross allowance carries a standing share set by the customer's Commercial Credit Account, the share being one of the percentages of the gross allowance: 0 percent where the account status is not active or the customer has no such account; 50 percent where the account is active and carries at least one returned-payment line dated within the 12 months before the request date.

An active account with no returned-payment line in that window carries no reduction under this rule.

### What the records show

- The account status is the status of the customer's Commercial Credit Account (active, or any other status such as on hold, in collections or closed).
- A returned-payment line is a credit account transaction recorded as a payment returned, dated by its transaction date; it is within the 12 months when fewer than 12 whole months separate its date from the request date (whole months being the difference in calendar months, less one where the day of the month of the later date is smaller).

### Truth table

| Account active | Returned-payment line within the 12 months | Standing share |
|---|---|---|
| no (or no account) | any | 0 percent |
| yes | one or more | 50 percent |
| yes | none | no reduction |

*Hypothetical cases:* a customer whose Commercial Credit Account is on hold carries a standing share of 0 percent, so the gross allowance is 0.00 whatever its purchase base. An active account with one payment returned eight months before the request carries 50 percent.
